lessons: High-performing hooks use extreme comparisons or surprising scale (e.g., Shark older than the US reached 185.1% retention at 10%; Tuna vs. Cod contrast reached 121.7%).

Avoid wordy, dense explanations immediately after the hook; dropping into heavy percentages or chemistry at ~10% timestamp causes major viewer drop-off (e.g., Garlic lost 34.2% at 0.10, Maple Syrup lost 34.8% at 0.10).
Never pause for viewer interaction; explicit prompts like 'Pause and guess...' cause direct viewer drop-off (lost 8.7% at 52% in Maple Syrup).

Avoid asking late-stage rhetorical questions or abstract prompts (e.g., 'Ever thought why...' questions caused end-video drops in Cold Water and Fruits Float; 'Now think about what happens...' dropped 10.4% in Prune Fingers).
Visual contrast topics hold viewers significantly better through the middle than abstract anatomical explanations (Tuna vs. Cod held 65.8% at 50%, while Prune Fingers dropped to 19.2% at 50%).
worst_moment_types: Immediate post-hook technical exposition and percentage stats (e.g., Maple Syrup, Garlic)
Engagement bait and forced pauses (e.g., 'Pause and guess...')
Abstract thought experiments or meta-prompts (e.g., 'Now think about what happens...')
Late-video rhetorical setup questions (e.g., 'Ever thought why...')
best_hook_types: Extreme historical/scale comparisons (e.g., 'This shark is older than the United States')
Direct visual side-by-side paradoxes (e.g., 'A bluefin tuna and a cod are both fish, but their meat looks like two completely different animals')
Visceral, personified action claims (e.g., 'Fresh pineapple is literally eating you back')
